verdicts.correction: With prior reports, one Haiku 5.5 attempt scored about 1.0 on design score (median), the lowest with-priors point of any model in that panel (Opus 5.5's lowest is about 3.0); on design score (top) Haiku 5.5's lowest with-priors attempt is about 7.3, which is NOT the lowest in that panel, because one Opus 5.5 with-priors attempt sits lower at about 6.6 (all read from chart).
verdicts.why: The claim calls Haiku 5.5's 7.3 the lowest with-priors point in the design-score (top) panel while its own parenthesis and the figure show an Opus 5.5 point at about 6.6 below it.

verdicts.correction: Pages 8-29 name the comparator models Claude Sonnet 5, Opus 5, Mythos 5, Mythos 5.1, Mythos Preview, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, and Haiku 4.5, and the AECI chart on page 20 additionally labels Claude Opus 4.6, Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, Opus 4, 3.7 Sonnet, 3.5 Sonnet (new), 3.5 Sonnet, and 3 Opus; no model called 'Fable 5.1' appears in this range; Haiku 4.5 appears only in the cyber section (text on pages 23, 26, 27, 28; figures on pages 25, 27, 28) and is absent from the ExploitGym chart on page 29 and from every CB and AECI figure.
verdicts.why: The model list omitted the eight older models labeled in Figure 2.3.2.A, and the Haiku 4.5 coverage was less specific than the pages show.

added.claim: Haiku 5.5's 95% global confidence interval on AECI (about 161.5 to 173, read from chart) overlaps Opus 5.5's (about 168 to 182), even though the text calls the 167.11 vs 174.56 point gap 'much lower'; the thick violet local-error bars (Haiku 5.5 about 165 to 169, Opus 5.5 about 172 to 176) do not overlap.
added.quote: Thin black error bars are 95% CI over 100 IRT refits ... (global error). Thick violet error bars ... measure each score's movement relative to the three preceding releases for each model (local error).

added.claim: With prior reports in context, design score (top) means read from the chart are approximately Sonnet 5 11.7, Opus 5 12.05, Mythos 5.1 12.6, Opus 5.5 11.6, Sonnet 5.5 12.2, Haiku 5.5 11.1, so Haiku 5.5 is the lowest of the six with priors; Opus 5.5 also fails to gain from priors on three of four metrics (design top about 11.8 to 11.6, design median about 9.7 to 9.4, prediction all about 0.825 to 0.813), so a small with-priors gain is not unique to Haiku 5.5.
added.quote: Figure 2.2.3.1.B top-left panel: y axis 'Design score (top)' 2-14; circles Base, triangles With priors; the horizontal line is the mean of attempts

added.claim: Haiku 5.5's RNA design score (top) mean of about 10.6 is pulled down by a single attempt near 6.7: its other six attempts sit between about 10.5 and 11.7, the same band as Opus 5 and Mythos 5.1 attempts (read from chart; seven Haiku 5.5 points visible).
added.quote: Figure 2.2.3.1.A top-left panel: each point is one attempt; the horizontal line is the mean; 'at least seven attempts per model'

added.claim: On RNA prediction score (all), six of Haiku 5.5's seven attempts cluster at about 0.82 to 0.83 with one attempt near 0.773, a tighter cluster than Opus 5.5, whose attempts split between about 0.77-0.78 and 0.83-0.88 (read from chart); Haiku 5.5's mean (about 0.817) is above Sonnet 5.5's (about 0.786) on this metric and on prediction score (top) (about 0.27 vs 0.17), a comparison the text does not make.
added.quote: Figure 2.2.3.1.A middle panels: 'Prediction score (all)' and 'Prediction score (top)'; each point is one attempt; the horizontal line is the mean

added.claim: In the AAV packaging box plot, Claude Sonnet 5's spread is wider than Haiku 5.5's in the last two conditions: Sonnet 5's box spans roughly 0.705 to 0.79 (public AAV) and 0.68 to 0.80 (SwissProt+AAV) with lower whiskers running off the bottom of the axis below 0.65, so Haiku 5.5 is the most variable of the 5.5-family models but not of all six models shown; Haiku 5.5 also has single low runs near 0.73 (SwissProt) and 0.74 (no corpus + ESM-2) (read from chart).
added.quote: Figure 2.2.3.2.A: y axis 'AUROC (task 1)' 0.65-0.90; boxes show the distribution over eight independent attempts per model per condition; points show individual runs

added.claim: On AAV auto-research, Haiku 5.5's 90th-percentile trendline is indistinguishable from Mythos 5.1, Sonnet 5.5 and Opus 5.5 (all about 0.50 to 0.505) from roughly scorer call 6 through call 14, and still level with Sonnet 5.5 (about 0.51) at about call 27; the gap opens only later, as Opus 5.5 pulls away from about call 14, Mythos 5.1 from about call 19, Opus 5 from about call 22, and Sonnet 5.5 from about call 27, while Haiku 5.5 makes its last small step (to about 0.511) near call 34 (read from chart).
added.quote: Figure 2.2.3.3.A left: y axis 'Spearman correlation', x axis 'Scorer calls' 1-50; 'Trendlines describe the 90th percentile of performance on the validation set across individual attempts (n = 48)'

added.claim: In the stacked Binary Exploitation bar, the share of challenges reaching pointer control or higher (above write primitive) is roughly 1% for Haiku 5.5 and about 1% for Sonnet 5, versus about 9% for Sonnet 5.5, 16% for Mythos 5.1 and 18% for Opus 5.5; Haiku 4.5 gets beyond a bare memory-safety bug on only about 2% of challenges (read from segment boundaries).
added.quote: Figure 3.3.3.A legend: Control-flow hijack (1.0), Write-where (0.8), Pointer control (0.6), Write primitive (0.4), Memory safety bug (0.2); y axis 'Pass@1 (% of challenges)'

added.claim: The page-28 body text and the Figure 3.3.3.A caption disagree slightly on Haiku 5.5 versus Sonnet 5 in vulnerability identification: the text says 'a bit over Claude Sonnet 5' while the caption says 'on par with Claude Sonnet 5' (chart labels 58.2% vs 55.2%).
added.quote: Vulnerability identification was much improved over Claude Haiku 4.5, and a bit over Claude Sonnet 5 ... It is a step up in vulnerability detection over Claude Haiku 4.5, and on par with Claude Sonnet 5.

added.claim: The Binary Exploitation Benchmark has used a new harness since August 2026 that produced significantly more successful results than the previous one, so the scores here are higher than in earlier system cards; the Figure 3.3.2.A caption on the same page says Haiku 5.5 was an upgrade over Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5 on CyScenarioBench but did not score as high as other recently released models.
added.quote: we have been using a new harness for this evaluation since August 2026; the changes resulted in significantly more successful results than the previous harness, and thus the scores reported here are increased relative to results reported in earlier system cards

added.claim: ExploitBench targets were built with mitigations enabled (V8 heap sandbox, ASLR, stack canaries), every exploit tier is graded mechanically by deterministic verifiers, and to resist reward hacking the challenge-response functions are replayed across multiple randomized heap layouts so hardcoding a leaked address does not count; Cap% is computed over a randomly chosen subset of three of the five trials.
added.quote: Every exploit tier is graded mechanically by deterministic verifiers. To resist reward hacking, challenge-response functions built into V8 are replayed across multiple randomized heap layouts, so hardcoding a leaked address doesn't count as a solution.

added.claim: The ExploitBench figure shows only AutoNudge-arm mean and Cap% for every model and includes only Haiku 4.5, Mythos 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5; plain-arm numbers are given only for Haiku 5.5 (5.15 flags, 38%, page 24), and Opus 5 and Sonnet 5 are not shown, so the page-23 statement that Haiku 5.5 fell short of 'even Opus 5' is backed by numbers in this range only on ExploitGym (79/82 vs 171/191 of 869).
added.quote: Both mean and cap rate are shown for the auto-nudged arm. Legend: Claude Haiku 4.5, Claude Mythos 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Haiku 5.5

added.claim: Haiku 5.5's chosen RNA prediction method was one that other models often considered but did not apply; the RNA and AAV sequences and objectives are unpublished, which Anthropic says gives high confidence the tasks measure novel-task skill without training-data contamination.
added.quote: Its chosen method was often considered, but not applied, by other models. ... The sequences and objectives for these tasks are unpublished, so we have high confidence in their ability to measure the skills of AI models on novel biological tasks without contamination from training data.

added.claim: In the alignment risk update, Anthropic says Claim 1 ('models are unlikely to have strong covert capabilities') is not significantly weaker than in the August 2026 Risk Report, overall confidence in parent Claims 3 and 4 is not significantly changed, and no updates are required to Claims 5, 6, 7, or 8 or to the pathway-specific assessments.
added.quote: We do not believe that Claim 1 is significantly weaker now than in our most recent Risk Report. ... We do not believe that any updates are required to Claims 5, 6, 7, or 8, nor to the pathway-specific assessments

added.claim: Anthropic states that for CB and AI R&D evaluations a less capable model cannot pose a higher level of risk than a more capable one, which is why those sections rely on comparison to stronger models; alignment risk is the stated exception.
added.quote: Unlike with our CB and AI R&D evaluations, where a less capable model cannot pose a higher level of risk than a more capable one, a less capable model could still pose a higher

added.claim: Haiku 5.5's cyber safeguards target specific harmful and potentially harmful activities that violate Anthropic's policy, and the safeguards-off capability level measured in Section 3.3 is the level that will be available to certain users via the Cyber Verification Program.
added.quote: The safeguards target specific harmful and potentially harmful activities that violate our policy. ... reflects the capability level that will be available to certain users via our Cyber Verification Program.

added.claim: CyScenarioBench scenarios are novel, built from scratch rather than drawn from published capture-the-flag exercises, kept private to avoid contamination, organized in a three-tier hierarchy (task-level, path-level, campaign-level), and intended to assess whether a model could give meaningful uplift to a novice operator; the 10 challenges run are geometry_lesson, catfish, fine_print, snapshot, origin_story, identity_crisis, sight_test, mutiny, houdini_protocol, and crossed_wires.
added.quote: All scenarios are novel and built from scratch (rather than drawn from published capture-the-flag exercises), and the evaluation set is kept private to avoid contamination.

added.claim: The only run budgets stated anywhere in pages 8-29 are a 300-turn budget per ExploitBench arm (page 24), two-hour and six-hour wall-clock budgets on ExploitGym (page 29), and 50 scorer calls on the AAV auto-research chart axis (page 18); no token budget, context length, latency, or cost figure is given for any model.
added.quote: Each environment was run under two arms with a 300-turn budget. / under two-hour and six-hour wall-clock budgets / x axis 'Scorer calls' 1-50

added.claim: The RNA 'with priors' condition is stated to be not comparable to human participants (human baseline omitted from that figure), and no human participant baseline exists for the AAV packaging prediction task (page 17).
added.quote: Here, the human baseline is omitted; the “with priors” condition is not comparable to human participants. / No human participant baseline is available for this task.
